# Notes on Ezekiel 1, verse by verse

**About these notes:** I ran out of searches before I could check several sites you listed: bibleodyssey.org, netbible.org (except NET notes quoted on Precept Austin), newadvent.org, wesley.nnu.edu, seedbed, the Lutheran sites and the Pentecostal sites (except Enduring Word). Ellicott's verse notes come from search snippets, because the page I opened only showed his introduction. I found nothing on prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace readings of this chapter. The Protestant "differences" below are mostly between individual commentators. I found no clear split between denominations.

---

## v. 1
- **Traditional reading:** The exact date shows this is a real event in a real place, not a fairy tale. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **"The heavens opened":** Poole, quoted by Guzik, says the passive wording shows a divine power did the opening. It was not a natural event in the sky. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **The heavens opening:** Coffman says Ezekiel is the only Old Testament prophet of whom this is said. In the New Testament it happens to Jesus, Stephen and John. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/ezekiel-1.html
- **"Visions of God":** Ellicott says this means visions sent by God, not simply "great visions." https://biblehub.com/ezekiel/1-1.htm
- **"The thirtieth year" (where commentators disagree):**
  - *Ezekiel's age (the most common view):* Barnes thinks it is probably his age, since 30 was when Levites began serving (Numbers 4). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-1.htm
  - The Pulpit Commentary agrees, following Origen and Hengstenberg. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/ezekiel-1.html
  - So does Constable, who also lists other options: Josiah's reform, a jubilee, and Nabopolassar's reign. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/ezekiel/1-1.html
  - *Calvin (Reformed):* He rejects counting from the finding of the Law. He argues the Jews counted from a jubilee. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/ezekiel/1-1.html
  - *Gill (Baptist, Calvinist):* He lists the jubilee, the Targum and Jerome, but prefers the thirtieth year of Nabopolassar. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/ezekiel/1-1.html
  - *Keil & Delitzsch:* They reject the age view because a month and day point to a known era. They say the era can no longer be identified for certain. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-1.htm
- **Modern scholarship (NET note):** The NET notes call the meaning "problematic." Origen took it as Ezekiel's age. The Aramaic Targum counted from the finding of the Torah scroll (2 Kings 22). https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel_11-14
- **Jewish practice:** Jamieson-Fausset-Brown (JFB) notes that later Jews forbade reading this book before age thirty. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-1.htm
- **Orthodox:** The OCA's life of the prophet says he had the vision at age thirty. https://www.oca.org/index.php/saints/lives/2022/07/21/102064-prophet-ezekiel

## v. 2
- **Dating:** Precept Austin says the double date in vv. 1–2 shows Ezekiel's care with dates. It places his call in 593 BC, in the fifth year of Jehoiachin's exile. https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel_11-14
- **Two eras matching:** Ellicott says the "fifth day" appearing with both datings shows the two eras began their years at the same time. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-1.htm
- **Modern scholarship:** One commentary on Bible Hub sees two headings here (v. 1 in Ezekiel's own voice, vv. 2–3 about him). It says they are joined awkwardly and may not be in their original form. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-1.htm

## v. 3
- **"Came directly":** Ellicott says the Hebrew repeats the verb for emphasis, meaning the word came with full proof that it was real. He adds that Ezekiel names himself only here and in 24:24. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/1.htm
- **"The LORD's hand":** Guzik says it shows Ezekiel was God's special agent, strengthened by Him. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **"The priest":** JFB says calling himself "the priest" marks his priestly role among the exiles. God would be a "little sanctuary" to them (11:16). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-1.htm
- **Kebar:** Ellicott's introduction identifies it with Nebuchadnezzar's royal canal, not the northern river Khabour. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/1.htm

## v. 4
- **North:** Guzik says the north was the direction of judgment and captivity. So even Babylon's rule over Israel came under God's control. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **Babylon's gods:** Guzik also says the vision assured Ezekiel that Yahweh rules all creation, however great Babylon's gods seemed. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **Gods of Babylon (McRae):** Allan McRae, quoted on Precept Austin, says a main purpose was to show that Israel's God matches and surpasses the splendour of Babylon's gods. https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel_115-28
- **Theme of the book:** Feinberg, quoted by Guzik, says Ezekiel's book centres on the glory of the Lord. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/

## v. 5
- **Identity:** Guzik says Ezekiel later calls these creatures cherubim (ch. 10). He links them to John's four creatures in Revelation 4. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **"Likeness":** Ellicott says the word makes plain that these were symbols seen in a vision, not actual creatures. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/1.htm
- **Matthew Henry:** He reads them as angels, God's servants doing His commands. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Eze/Eze_001.cfm

## v. 6
- **Faces and wings:** catholic.com walks through the four faces and four wings and notes Ezekiel calls them cherubim in ch. 10. https://www.catholic.com/audio/tjap/the-tetramorph-4-mysterious-symbols

## v. 7
- **Feet:** Ellicott says the calf-like sole was round and solid, not made to move only forward like a human foot. The gleam refers only to the hoof. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/1.htm

## v. 8
- **Hands:** Ellicott says the human hands add to the creatures' human look. There were four hands per cherub, matching the wings, which were attached at the shoulder. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/1.htm

## v. 9
- **Throne chariot:** Utley (bible.org) calls this a vision of God's mobile throne chariot. He notes 1 Chronicles 28:18 links the ark with a chariot. https://bible.org/book/export/html/20223

## v. 10
- **What the faces mean (traditional):** Smith, quoted by Guzik, says man is the highest creature, and the lion, ox and eagle rule the wild animals, tame animals and skies. All creation is under God's throne. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **Ligonier (Reformed):** The faces stand for God's power, wisdom, swiftness and life-giving nature. Other ancient peoples combined animals in art, but never all four of these. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/ezekiels-vision-god
- **Catholic (catholic.com):** The man, lion, ox and eagle are the source of the "tetramorph" (the four symbols of the Gospel writers). Irenaeus was apparently the first to link them to the Gospels: Matthew as man, Mark as eagle, Luke as ox, John as lion. The writer stresses that in Ezekiel's literal sense they are throne attendants, not the Evangelists. Different writers have matched them up differently. https://www.catholic.com/audio/tjap/the-tetramorph-4-mysterious-symbols
- **Orthodox (OCA):** The four creatures are the Evangelists: man for Matthew, lion for Mark, ox for Luke, eagle for John. https://www.oca.org/index.php/saints/lives/2022/07/21/102064-prophet-ezekiel
- **Evangelical:** GotQuestions traces the tetramorph to Irenaeus and to its wide use in Christian art. https://www.gotquestions.org/tetramorph.html

## v. 11
- **Wings:** catholic.com explains that two wings touched the next creature's wings and two modestly covered the body. https://www.catholic.com/audio/tjap/the-tetramorph-4-mysterious-symbols

## v. 12
- **Going straight ahead:** Matthew Henry applies this to the angels' sincere aim at God's glory, with no hidden motives. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Eze/Eze_001.cfm
- **"The spirit":** Precept Austin notes that no major translation capitalises "spirit." It still thinks reading it as the Holy Spirit is reasonable. https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel_115-28

## v. 13
- **Fire:** A Bible Hub article says the creatures' burning look shows God's consuming holiness (Hebrews 12:29). https://biblehub.com/q/Symbolism_of_Ezekiel_s_creatures.htm

## v. 14
- **Lightning:** Guzik says the overall impression is constant motion, both of the creatures and of the throne. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/

## v. 15
- **A chariot:** Guzik says the picture is hard to draw but probably shows a great four-wheeled chariot carrying God's throne. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **Placement:** Barnes places one wheel directly beneath each creature, made to move in any of the four directions. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-16.htm

## v. 16
- **Shape of the wheel (common view):** Ellicott, Barnes and Keil all picture two rings at right angles, like the equator and a meridian on a globe. This lets the wheel go any way without turning. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-16.htm
- **NET note:** Some think the rings were one inside the other, others a globe shape. Verse 17 favours the globe. https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel_115-28
- **The wheels as God's providence:**
  - *Matthew Henry:* God's providence often looks dark and confusing to us, but is ordered for the best. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-16.htm
  - *Calvin (Reformed):* God keeps a steady course in Himself while turning the world. That is why the wheels seem tangled together. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/ezekiel/1-16.html
  - *Spurgeon (Baptist):* The wheels are Providence. Life's fortunes go up and down, but God's love to His people is the fixed axle at the centre. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/ezekiel/1-18.html
- **Gill (Baptist), a different application:** The four matching wheels stand for the true churches of Christ, which share the same faith, ordinances and government. He insists the wheels were the same size and crossed each other. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-16.htm
- **Debated popular teaching (UFOs):**
  - Chuck Smith (Calvary Chapel) compares the movement to reports of how flying saucers move. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/ezekiel/1-18.html
  - Precept Austin calls the UFO reading "absurd," because Ezekiel names the sight as the glory of the LORD. https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel_115-28

## v. 17
- **Ark and temple:** Craigie, quoted on Precept Austin, says the cherubim recall those above the ark, which was itself called a chariot. So Ezekiel learned that being cut off from Jerusalem did not mean being cut off from God. https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel_115-28

## v. 18
- **Eyes:** The eyes picture God, who sees everything; nothing is hidden from Him (2 Chronicles 16:9, Proverbs 15:3). https://www.preceptaustin.org/ezekiel_115-28
- **GotQuestions:** The wheels' movement suggests God is everywhere, the eyes that He knows everything, and their height His power. https://www.gotquestions.org/Ezekiel-wheels.html
- **Orthodox:** The OCA says the many-eyed wheel suggests light being shared with all nations. https://www.oca.org/index.php/saints/lives/2022/07/21/102064-prophet-ezekiel

## vv. 19–21
- **"The spirit … in the wheels":** Keil says this is the spirit of the creatures, seen as one unit. It is not a general "life principle." The spirit fully controls the wheels' going, stopping and rising. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ezekiel/1-16.htm
- **GotQuestions:** Most scholars hold that God's Spirit directed the wheels. https://www.gotquestions.org/Ezekiel-wheels.html
- **Matthew Henry:** The same wisdom that governs the angels governs events on earth, even through people who do not intend it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/ezekiel/1-18.html

## v. 22
- **The expanse:** Leithart (Gospel Coalition) sees the vision as a small model of the world. The creatures are below, a sky-like "firmament" (expanse) is above them, and the throne is above that. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/ezekiel-vision/
- **Bridgeway:** It is a shining platform holding up God's throne. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/ezekiel/1-1.html

## v. 23
- **Wings:** Ellicott says the King James wording confuses things. Each creature had two wings covering its body, one on either side. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/1.htm

## v. 24
- **Sound of the wings:** Ellicott would translate "voice" throughout this verse. The same "many waters" comparison describes God's voice in 43:2 and Revelation 1:15. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/1.htm

## v. 25
- **The voice:** Matthew Henry says that when the voice sounded from the expanse, Ezekiel looked up, as John did in Revelation 1. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Eze/Eze_001.cfm

## v. 26
- **"Likeness":** Guzik says Ezekiel saw only the likeness of the throne and of God, not the things themselves. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **A man's form:** Feinberg says the human form is the highest symbol available. God's supreme self-revelation came in the Man Christ Jesus. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **Pointing to Christ:**
  - *Matthew Henry:* Ezekiel saw "one like unto the Son of man." https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Eze/Eze_001.cfm
  - *Barnes:* The vision is fulfilled in Christ. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/ezekiel/1-1.html
  - *Coffman:* It parallels Exodus 24:10 and has overtones of the Incarnation. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/ezekiel-1.html
- **Ligonier:** The scene recalls God's throne room in Exodus 24. God is about to go out from His usual dwelling. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/ezekiels-vision-god
- **Leithart:** The throne is the heart of the vision. The cherubim and wheels only carry the One enthroned. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/ezekiel-vision/
- **Orthodox:** The Fathers say the human likeness on the throne foreshadows the Incarnation from the Virgin Mary, who is the living Throne of God. https://www.oca.org/index.php/saints/lives/2022/07/21/102064-prophet-ezekiel

## v. 27
- **Fire above and below:** Guzik says the fire coming downward suggests God's power reaching from heaven to earth. God is high above, yet still directs His creation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **Unlike idols:** A writer quoted by Guzik says Yahweh's radiance comes from His own being, unlike idols that need polishing. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/

## v. 28
- **The rainbow:** Guzik says a throne declares God's power, while the rainbow (God's promise to Noah) shows that He limits Himself by His own promises. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **Bible Hub:** It is a sign of mercy and covenant faithfulness in the middle of judgment. https://biblehub.com/ezekiel/1-28.htm
- **Piled-up words:** Ellicott notes "likeness" and "appearance" are repeated throughout. Ezekiel is stressing that he saw symbols, not the reality itself. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/ellicott/ezekiel/1.htm
- **Expositor's:** What Ezekiel saw is only an imperfect copy of God's glory, which no human eye can look on. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/teb/ezekiel-1.html
- **"Glory":** The Hebrew word *kabod* comes from a root meaning "heavy," pointing to the weight of God's majesty. https://www.blueletterbible.org/comm/guzik_david/study-guide/ezekiel/ezekiel-1.cfm
- **Falling down:** Guzik says Ezekiel's response was humble surrender, and God then revealed Himself by His word. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/ezekiel-1/
- **Not tied to Jerusalem:** Coffman says the vision shows God was as present in Babylon as in the temple. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/bcc/ezekiel-1.html

---

## The whole chapter: Jewish "Merkavah" tradition
- **Gospel Coalition (Leithart):** Jewish mysticism treated Ezekiel's chariot ("Merkabah") as a path up to God's throne. Leithart says Ezekiel shows the opposite: the throne coming down from heaven to earth. https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/article/ezekiel-vision/
- **Matthew Henry:** The rabbis called this vision *Mercabah*, the vision of the chariot. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Eze/Eze_010.cfm
- **Orthodox:** An OCA report mentions a talk comparing Orthodox hesychast prayer with Jewish Merkavah meditation on this vision. https://www.oca.org/reflections/fr.-john-jillions/september-16-2014
